items.html:
Source confirmed at fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d; checkout HEAD matched throughout inspection. No execution probes or changes.

Recommendation: functional dispatch for sphere_tmatrix, slab, and plane_wave is a useful bounded first step, provided it includes deliberate promotion of ordinary constant incident plane waves. Reuse existing framework objects and adapters. A new explicit namespace adds little because import treams_rs as tr; backend = tr.advect already works lazily.

Evidence:

  • Correct namespace is treams_rs, not upstream treams: init.py:3; native module is treams_rs._native, pyproject.toml:114.
  • Root documents NumPy/non-tracing behavior and CPU first-order adapter behavior: init.py:62. Optional modules load on access via __getattr__, retaining ordinary root startup: init.py:208. Optional dependency declarations: pyproject.toml:65.

Ordinary calls cross several distinct boundaries:

Surface Source-confirmed behavior Consequence
Material construction complex() on epsilon, mu, kappa: _material.py:41 Dispatch after construction is too late for dynamic materials.
TMatrix construction np.array/np.asarray, positive-frequency validation then float(k0), read-only ndarray ownership: _tmatrix.py:92, _validation.py:38 Existing ordinary classes are NumPy contracts, not array-neutral containers.
Sphere classmethod Converts every layer to ordinary Material, calls diff.sphere, drops context: _tmatrix.py:726 Retaining NumPy array arithmetic alone cannot connect Rust derivatives.
Ordinary class methods Cross sections explicitly return Python floats: _tmatrix.py:385; average values likewise: _tmatrix.py:667 Replacing one native call does not make the whole class traceable.
coeffs.mie Calls diff.mie(...)[0]: coeffs.py:110 Existing record can be reused, but ordinary wrapper discards derivative context.
Genuine ufunc exports special.jv directly aliases native ufunc; documented out, where, ufunc methods: special.py:134 Replacing with a plain Python dispatch wrapper changes public ufunc identity/methods unless deliberately scoped.
Ufunc-like wrappers sw.translate selects and calls native ufunc: sw.py:112; cw.rotate has Python-scalar fast path: cw.py:105 Dispatch must preserve scalar fast paths and NumPy out/where semantics.
Native Rust records Sphere takes f64 and NumPy readonly arrays, returns NumPy value plus context; pullback returns five gradients: tmatrix.rs:23, tmatrix.rs:46 Array protocols alone do not attach this pullback to an AD graph.

diff.sphere performs contiguous NumPy conversion (diff.py:1194); this is appropriate inside existing adapter callbacks, not before selecting them. The framework sphere path already preserves materials as arrays and applies the record: _framework.py:261. Its TMatrix and methods retain _backend: _framework_tmatrix.py:34, _framework_tmatrix.py:90.

Critical constant-input trap: a radius tracer can select the sphere adapter, while tr.plane_wave([0,0,1], "positive_helicity", k0=2.0) has no backend-valued input and returns an ordinary PlaneWave. It cannot currently enter framework cross_sections:

  • Ordinary in_basis accepts only basis: _waves.py:423.
  • Framework caller supplies positions and singular, then checks _backend: _framework_tmatrix.py:23, _framework_backend.py:388.
  • Framework method accepts those parameters: _framework_waves.py:265.
  • Slab power identifies incident side using isinstance(framework PlaneWave) before _incident; promotion must happen before side detection: _framework_smatrix.py:188.

A narrow constant-wave promotion is feasible: ordinary PlaneWave exposes direction, coefficients, k0, medium and polarization. Initially support fixed real-direction helicity waves, matching the framework constructor’s actual limits ( _framework_waves.py:233). Preserve that wave’s own constants; do not replace its k0/medium with the response’s dynamic values. Raw scalar/tuple dynamic materials can go directly through factories; dynamic root Material remains unsupported until its constructor changes.

Classmethod compatibility needs an explicit boundary. Root sphere_tmatrix and multilayer_sphere_tmatrix delegate to TMatrix.sphere ( _tmatrix.py:921). That classmethod has its own legacy signature with exterior included in materials ( _tmatrix.py:703). Dispatching only factories leaves classmethods NumPy-only. Dispatching the classmethod itself returns the separate framework class and cannot promise cls/subclass identity. Document functional factories as the initial supported API.

Meaningful later checks: radius/epsilon sphere scattering and thickness/epsilon slab transmission against existing explicit namespaces; constant incidents created inside/outside objectives; dynamic frequency shared between response and source; mixed backends rejected; nested materials; parity and unsupported directions; class return types; ordinary NumPy import timing and scalar/array latency; preservation of out/where/ufunc identity if low-level scope is later added. No need to change Rust formulas for dispatch itself.
